items.title: 66086_Zilner T. Randolph oral history interview
items.q: I was to go into Regal Theater with Jerome Carrington

ctx.x: When you first came to Chicago -- I've done some reading about this -- and it seems like there were three kinds of jobs. There was theater jobs, ballroom jobs, and then cabaret jobs, where the small bands played. And there seemed to be some resistence among the theater and ballroom leaders, such as Doc Cook, Charlie Elgar, Dave Peyton, to the cabaret musicians -- a lot of the New Orleans musicians didn't were there because, I guess, because they couldn't read so well. Did you sense any of this?

No, because I guess I was busy trying to weather the storm of my own thing by being transfer member from Milwaukee in here, and it looked like this union had it in for transfer members, because I was to go into Regal Theater with Jerome Carrington and I think George Smith was president
and he didn't let me go.
